headline: Tanzania Opens First Protected Wildlife Corridor for Elephants
meta_description: Tanzania's first officially protected wildlife corridor gives elephants a safer route between historic habitats, with 529 already using the 14-km passage.
summary_short: A new 14-kilometer protected corridor in Tanzania is helping elephants move safely between traditional habitats. Nearly 530 have already used it.
body:
Tanzania has officially opened its first protected wildlife corridor, creating a safer passage for elephants moving between their historic habitats. So far, 529 elephants have already been recorded using the 14-kilometer route.

The corridor's success hinges on an act of shared stewardship: 368 landowners voluntarily gave up portions of their land to allow the passage to exist. This cooperation between private landholders and conservation efforts demonstrates how elephants can coexist with human communities when communities choose to protect their movement.

The corridor addresses a critical challenge facing elephants across Africa—habitat fragmentation that forces them into dangerous encounters with human settlements and infrastructure. By creating this officially protected route, Tanzania has given one of Africa's most iconic species a documented, safer way to follow migration patterns shaped over centuries.
quick_facts: Tanzania's first officially protected wildlife corridor spans 14 kilometers
529 elephants recorded using the new passage so far
368 landowners voluntarily contributed land for the corridor
